title: Coming soon: Gmail to Notion summariser (Make.com)
description: An end-to-end Make.com flow that watches a Gmail label, summarises every new email with Claude, and appends the summary to a Notion database. Saves 30 minutes a day on inbox triage. Launching with our first 5 templates in June.
toolTips: Coming soon. Sign up for the newsletter and we will send you the JSON template the moment it lands.
content:
Status: coming soon (June 2026).

This automation will:

  1. Watch a Gmail label of your choice (e.g. 'Newsletters', 'Customer feedback', 'Sales replies').
  2. For every new email, run the body through Claude with a summarisation prompt.
  3. Append the summary, sender, and original link to a Notion database row.
  4. Optionally tag it with sentiment (positive/neutral/negative) so you can spot patterns.

You will get the importable Make.com JSON, a 5-minute video walking through the setup, and the exact Claude prompt we use.

To get notified when it launches: sign up for the weekly newsletter from any signup box on this site.
howToUse: Sign up to the newsletter to be first in line
Bundle members get every automation template free as part of lifetime access
whyItWorks: Email is the highest-friction inbox most knowledge workers face. The summariser flips the cost of skimming from O(n) to O(1) - one glance at Notion is enough to know which thread deserves your attention. We use this exact flow internally.
makeItYourOwn: Replace the Notion database with a Slack channel, an Airtable base, or a Google Sheet. Replace the Claude summariser with GPT-4o mini for cheaper runs at scale. Add a webhook trigger so you can manually run it on a single email.

title: Coming soon: RSS feed to LinkedIn carousel (n8n)
description: An n8n workflow that watches an RSS feed (your blog, a competitor's blog, an industry newsletter) and turns each new post into a 5-slide LinkedIn carousel ready for review. Cuts content repurposing from 30 mins to 3.
toolTips: Coming soon. The template will work with any blog that has an RSS feed - WordPress, Ghost, Webflow, or our own /blog feed.
content:
Status: coming soon (June 2026).

This automation will:

  1. Watch an RSS feed for new posts.
  2. Extract the headline, key points, and a closing thought.
  3. Generate 5 slide-ready snippets (hook, point 1, point 2, point 3, CTA) in Claude.
  4. Drop them into a Google Doc named after the post, ready for you to copy into Canva or Figma.

Includes the n8n workflow JSON, a 5-minute install video, and a prompt template you can fork for X threads or Instagram Reels.
howToUse: Sign up to the newsletter to be notified when it launches
Bundle members get every automation template free as part of lifetime access
whyItWorks: The hard bit of repurposing is not the writing. It is deciding what to keep and what to cut. By forcing a 5-slide structure with named beats (hook, points, CTA), the workflow does the editorial work. You only review.
makeItYourOwn: Replace LinkedIn carousels with X threads (5 tweets), Instagram Reels scripts, or a daily Slack digest. Filter the RSS by category if your source is a multi-author site. Add a translation step if you publish in two languages.

title: Coming soon: Calendar block to weekly summary (Zapier)
description: A Zapier flow that watches a calendar block (e.g. 'Deep work block', '1:1 with Sarah', 'Customer call') and writes a weekly summary of how you spent your time, who you spent it with, and what came out of each block.
toolRecommendation: Zapier (free tier supports this for one calendar)
toolTips: Coming soon. Will work with Google Calendar and Microsoft 365.
content:
Status: coming soon (June 2026).

This automation will:

  1. Watch your calendar for events tagged with specific keywords (e.g. 'Deep work', 'Customer call', '1:1').
  2. At the end of each week, compile the events by tag.
  3. Run them through Claude with a summarisation prompt that produces a polished weekly recap.
  4. Drop the recap into a Notion page or send it to you in Slack.

Includes the Zapier template, a one-page PDF of the prompt we use, and a sample output.
howToUse: Sign up to the newsletter to be notified
Bundle members get every automation template free
whyItWorks: Most people end the week with a vague sense of how they spent it. This flow turns 'busy week' into 'spent 14 hours on customer calls, 6 on deep work, 3 on internal meetings' - which makes time-budget conversations with yourself or your manager actually possible.
makeItYourOwn: Add a sentiment dimension so the summary flags weeks where you spent more than 30% of time in low-energy categories. Pipe the output into a personal coaching journal. Use the same trigger to drive automatic CRM updates after every 'Customer call' tagged event.
